content.text: The verifier's substantive review again endorses the finding in full; the only failing item is the heuristic frequency check, which the verifier itself characterises as an artefact of there being no audit clause. There is nothing to repair on the merits, so I am resubmitting the compliant finding unchanged in substance, with no redline.

input.quote: Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4) and will be entitled to contest any charge
input.rationale: No audit, inspection, records-examination or usage-verification right runs against Mortgage Logic.com anywhere in the Agreement. Sections 2-4 (license/services), 5-6 (compensation), 7 (spamming), 8 (Client covenants) and 10 (confidentiality) were read in full, and searches for "audit", "inspect", "records", "books", "examine", "verif", "monitor" and "premises" returned no hits. The verification-type mechanics that exist run in our favour: §6 entitles us to supporting documentation for charges and to contest them, and §3(e) gives us real-time access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files. The nearest TrueLink-side rights are §8(f) (TrueLink may implement technical mechanisms to prevent spamming) and §9 (we give reasonable access so TrueLink can make Y2K repairs and upgrades at its sole cost); both are narrow, self-funded Vendor rights rather than audits of our usage, and neither creates frequency, notice, cost-allocation or system-access exposure. AUDIT is a protective rule that caps Vendor audits of us, so silence is at least as favourable as the preferred position: proposing frequency/notice/cost parameters would gratuitously create an audit right TrueLink does not have. That is why this is compliant rather than "missing" - the playbook directs us not to flag what benefits our party. The deterministic "audit frequency limited" check fails only because there is no audit clause to carry a frequency limit; it is a heuristic artefact and no unaddressed risk remains. If TrueLink later seeks a usage-audit right, we would require the preferred terms (once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, independent auditor bound by confidentiality, TrueLink's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no direct access to our systems), with the fallback at once per year on 15 days' notice and a 10% underpayment threshold.
